reasons.plausibility: Aluminum has very limited solubility in refractory BCC alloys and strongly tends to form brittle intermetallics (e.g., B2, Laves phases) with Zr, Ti, and Hf, making retention of a single-phase BCC structure and high strength highly unlikely.
reasons.testability: The proposed experiment is well-defined with clear quantitative rejection criteria (density reduction <10%, strength drop >10%, secondary phase formation), making it directly falsifiable.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses the core trade-off but proposes a widely known problematic alloying strategy (Al in refractory BCC) without acknowledging prior evidence of embrittlement, limiting its practical value.
